name: canli-markets-mcp

tools.name: verify_claims
tools.description: Check a draft answer's figures against the company's own filings before using them: revenue, net income, EPS, operating income, margins, growth, cash flow, assets, debt and more, for a fiscal year or quarter as the company labels it. US and foreign filers (20-F, IFRS), in their own currency. Each claim comes back confirmed, contradicted (with the filed figure and what the claimed one matches instead: another year, a quarter, a unit slip), not reported or not checkable.

company.description: Ticker (AAPL, NVO, TSM), CIK (320193) or name: the company the claims are about. Foreign companies filing 20-F or 40-F are checked too, in the currency they report in.

claims.description: Claims to check, each a measure, period and value.

measure.description: What the figure is: revenue, net income, diluted EPS, operating income, gross profit, operating margin, net margin, free cash flow, total assets, cash, long-term debt, R&D, dividends per share...

period.description: The period as the company labels it: "fiscal 2025", "FY2025", "2025", "Q3 2026", "third quarter of fiscal 2026", or a span by its end date: "three months ended June 28, 2025".

value.description: The claimed figure, as written: 416.2 with unit "USD billion"; margins and growth in percent.

unit.description: "USD billion", "EUR million", "DKK billion", "USD per share", "%". A currency the company does not report in is a conversion and is not judged.

growth.description: The value is growth over the prior year, in percent.

basis.description: Adjusted and non-GAAP figures are not in the XBRL statements and are not checked here.

text.description: Or a draft answer about the company: every figure in it with a measure and a period is checked.

tools.name: european_filings
tools.description: A European company's annual financial report as it filed it in the European Single Electronic Format (ESEF): revenue, operating and net profit, EPS, assets, equity, cash, cash flows and dividends as the company tagged them (IFRS concepts, its currency, full scale), with the comparatives, the report's viewer link and the other years on file. Issuers on EU and EEA regulated markets, found by name or LEI; words find any other tagged figure.

company.description: Company name (ASML, LVMH, TotalEnergies) or its LEI (724500Y6DUVHQD6OXN27).

year.description: Fiscal year the report covers (the year its period ends); default the latest filed.

words.description: Also find the report's other figures whose concept names hold these words ("net system sales", "lease liabilities").

tools.name: reference_rates
tools.description: Money-market and policy rates from the central banks themselves: SOFR, TGCR, BGCR, EFFR and OBFR from the New York Fed (with percentiles and volume), the euro short-term rate and the ECB's policy rates, SONIA and Bank Rate from the Bank of England, and about forty central banks' policy rates as the BIS collects them (policy:JP, policy:Brazil). Dates and rates, oldest first.

rate.description: sofr, tgcr, bgcr, effr or obfr (New York Fed); estr, ecb_deposit, ecb_refi or ecb_marginal (ECB); sonia or bank_rate (Bank of England); or policy:<country>, a central bank's policy rate as the BIS collects it (policy:JP, policy:Brazil, policy:euro area).

start.description: First date; default 90 days before end.

tools.name: prediction_markets
tools.description: What traders on Polymarket and Kalshi are paying for an outcome, found by words (a Fed decision, a recession, an election, a price level): each market's probability (the middle of bid and ask, else the last trade), bid, ask, volume and closing date, with the event's resolution rules.

query.description: What the market is about, in words: "fed rate cut", "recession 2026", "bitcoin 150k".

tools.name: crypto_fundamentals
tools.description: A DeFi protocol's total value locked (now, by chain, and its history), the fees users pay it and the revenue it keeps (24 hours to all time); a chain's total value locked; or a stablecoin's supply in circulation and its change, by chain. From DefiLlama's open data.

protocol.description: A DeFi protocol by name or DefiLlama slug: aave, lido, uniswap, maker, pendle.

chain.description: A chain's total value locked: Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum, Base.

stablecoin.description: A stablecoin's supply in circulation: USDT, USDC, DAI, USDe.

days.description: Days of history to return; default 365.

tools.name: financial_statements
tools.description: A company's financial statements exactly as filed: income statement, balance sheet, cash flow and equity statement from its 10-K (or 10-Q), with its own line labels, each line's XBRL concept and the values as the filing shows them (units say the scale). Joins several filings by period; a line a later filing restated, or that a stock split changed, is shown beside its first-reported figure, never mixed in.

statement.description: Which statement: income, balance_sheet, cash_flow, comprehensive_income, equity; core (default) is the first three, all is every one.

period.description: annual (10-K, default) or quarterly (10-Q: each quarter and the year to date; the fourth quarter is only in the 10-K's year).

filings.description: How many 10-Ks (or 10-Qs) to read and join by period, newest first; default 1. One 10-K holds three years of income and cash flows and two balance sheets, so 2 covers four years and 3 covers five.

fiscal_year.description: Start from the 10-K for the fiscal year ending in this calendar year (or the latest 10-Q of it).

filed_before.description: Start from the latest filing on or before this date: what was known then.

tools.name: filing_tables
tools.description: The table in a filing that holds a figure, found by words ("paid members", "revenue by region", "guidance"): XBRL statement and detail reports and the tables in the document itself (MD&A figures such as members, stores or ARPU), or an 8-K press release's tables. With filings above one, the same words in each earlier filing, to follow a figure over the years. Without words, lists the tables.

find.description: Words the table holds, in its title or its row labels: "paid members", "revenue by region", "share repurchases", "adjusted EPS reconciliation"; quote a phrase. Without find, the filing's tables are listed.

form.description: 10-K (default), 10-Q, 8-K (a results press release's tables), DEF 14A (proxy), 20-F, S-1...

filings.description: Look in this many filings of the form, newest first, to follow a figure over the years; default 1. Needs find.

filed_before.description: Start from the latest filing of the form on or before this date.

document.description: Search this document of the filing instead (by type or file name, "EX-99.2"); default the main document, or an 8-K's press release.

max_tables.description: Most tables shown per filing; default 3.

tools.name: earnings_release
tools.description: A quarter's results press release (8-K Item 2.02): the headline, the results it states (each with the part of the business it belongs to and what a change is measured against), its guidance parsed into ranges (low, high, midpoint, unit, measure, basis, period, and the sentence or table row), and the previous release's guidance for this quarter set against the company's results: above, within or below the range, in basis points for rates.

accession.description: A results 8-K; default the latest (earnings_calendar lists them).

filed_before.description: The latest results release filed on or before this date.

compare.description: Line up the previous release's guidance for this quarter against these results; default true.

tools.name: screen_companies
tools.description: Screen every US-listed company (thousands, from SEC XBRL frames) on fundamentals: revenue, growth, margins, ROE, ROA, free cash flow, R&D intensity, leverage and more, for a calendar year or each company's fiscal year ending in a date window, with filters, ranking and optional valuation (price, market cap, P/E, P/S, FCF yield). Implausible figures (tagging slips) are held out and listed apart.

period.description: FY2025 (each company's fiscal year that best overlaps calendar 2025; default the last complete year) or a quarter such as CY2026Q2.

fiscal_year_end.description: Instead of period: each company's fiscal year ending between these dates, e.g. ["2025-02-01", "2026-01-31"]; balance-sheet figures at that year's end.

value.description: A number, or [low, high] for between. Ratios and growth are fractions (0.2 = 20%); money in US dollars.

sort_by.description: Metric to rank by; default the first filter's metric, else revenue.

exchanges.description: Listing venues to include; default NYSE and Nasdaq. "all" includes unlisted filers.

valuation.description: Add price, market cap, P/E, P/S and FCF yield for the returned companies (latest close; up to 50 companies).

include_suspect.description: Keep companies whose figures fail a plausibility check (for example net income above 10 times revenue, usually a tagging slip); default false: they are listed apart.

tools.name: company_report
tools.description: One company in one call: profile, five fiscal years of financials (revenue, growth, margins, net income, EPS, cash flow, ROE, leverage), price and risk over a year (return, volatility, drawdown, beta), valuation (market cap, P/E, P/S, FCF yield), insider buying and selling, and recent filings, each from its source.

tools.name: event_study
tools.description: How a stock's price reacted to events: earnings releases (8-K item 2.02), insider purchases or sales (Form 4), any 8-K, or given dates. Abnormal returns against a market model, cumulative abnormal return per event and on average, with a t test across events.

events.description: Event dates (day 0 is that date, or the next trading day). Leave out to use event_type.

event_type.description: Events from SEC filings: earnings (8-K item 2.02), open-market insider purchases or sales (Form 4 codes P or S, at filing time), or any 8-K. Day 0 is the first trading session after the filing was accepted.

since.description: For event_type: filings since this date; default three years ago.

window.description: Event window in trading days around day 0; default [-1, 5].

estimation_days.description: Days used to fit the model, ending 10 days before the window; default 120.

benchmark.description: Market index for the model; default SPY.

model.description: market (OLS alpha and beta on the benchmark, default), market_adjusted (return minus benchmark) or mean_adjusted.

tools.name: mentions_trend
tools.description: How often a word or phrase appears in SEC filings over time (by month, quarter or year), across all filers or one company, from EDGAR full-text search: for themes such as "tariffs", "agentic AI" or "going concern".

query.description: Words or a quoted phrase, for example "\"artificial intelligence\"" or tariffs.

start.description: First day; default three years ago.

tools.name: company_profile
tools.description: A company's or fund's SEC profile by ticker, CIK or name: tickers, exchange, industry (SIC), fiscal year end, state, address, former names, and its latest 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K and 13F.

tools.name: list_filings
tools.description: A company's SEC filings, newest first, filtered by form type (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, DEF 14A, S-1, 4, 13F-HR...) and dates, with links. Use read_filing to read one.

forms.description: Form types, for example ["10-K", "8-K"]; amendments (10-K/A) are included. Default: all.

since.description: Filed on or after this date.

until.description: Filed on or before this date.

tools.name: read_filing
tools.description: The text of an SEC filing: the latest of a form, or one by accession. For a 10-K or 10-Q, section returns one item ("risk factors", "md&a", "business", "market risk", "legal proceedings", or a number such as "1A"); without it the result lists the items and their lengths. document reads an exhibit, such as an 8-K's press release ("EX-99.1"). find returns only the passages with given words ("employees", "buyback"), the fastest way to a fact in a long filing; otherwise long text pages with offset.

accession.description: The filing; from list_filings or search_filings.

form.description: Without accession: read the company's latest filing of this form; default 10-K.

filed_before.description: Without accession: the latest filing of the form filed on or before this date.

section.description: 10-K or 10-Q item: "risk factors", "md&a", "business", "market risk", "legal proceedings", "1A", "7"; the result lists every item found.

document.description: Another document in the filing, by file name or type, for example "EX-99.1" (an 8-K's press release).

find.description: Words to find in the filing (or section), for example "employees" or "share repurchase": returns the matching passages with their offsets instead of the text from the start. Quote a phrase to match it exactly.

offset.description: Character offset to continue from; the previous result's next_offset, or a find match's offset.

tools.name: search_filings
tools.description: Full-text search across all SEC filings since 2001 (EDGAR full-text search): which companies mention a phrase, filtered by form, filer and dates. Quote phrases.

query.description: Words to find in filing text; put a phrase in double quotes, for example "\"supply chain\" tariffs".

forms.description: Form types, for example ["10-K"]. Default: all.

tools.name: insider_trades
tools.description: Insider transactions at a company from its Form 4 filings: who (officers, directors, 10% owners), what (open-market buys and sales, option exercises, tax withholding, gifts), shares, price, value, holdings after, and 10b5-1 plan flags, with a buy/sell summary. Default: the last 90 days.

since.description: Filed on or after; default 90 days ago.

until.description: Filed on or before; default today.

codes.description: Transaction codes to keep, for example ["P", "S"] for open-market purchases and sales. Default: all.

max_filings.description: Most Form 4 filings to read, newest first; default 40.

tools.name: fund_holdings
tools.description: A fund manager's 13F holdings for a quarter (latest by default): positions by value with portfolio weights, the total checked against the filing's cover page, and what changed since the previous quarter (new, exited, added, reduced).

manager.description: The 13F filer: name ("Berkshire Hathaway", "Bridgewater Associates"), ticker or CIK.

period.description: Quarter end, for example 2026-06-30; default the latest filed.

top.description: Most positions to list, by value; default 25.

compare.description: Also compare with the previous quarter's filing; default true.

tools.name: treasury_yields
tools.description: US Treasury daily yields from the Treasury itself: the par yield curve (1 month to 30 years), real (TIPS) yields or bill rates, for the latest day, a date, or a date range. In percent.

curve.description: nominal (par yield curve, 1 month to 30 years; default), real (TIPS), or bills.

date.description: One day (the latest on or before it). Default: the latest published.

start.description: A range instead of one day: first date.

end.description: Last date of the range; default today.

tools.name: economic_series
tools.description: Any FRED economic series (inflation, unemployment, GDP, payrolls, rates, credit spreads, oil, FX, money supply, recession indicators) by id or plain words, as dates and values, optionally as changes or year-over-year rates. Feed values straight into analysis tools.

series.description: A FRED series id (DGS10, CPIAUCSL, UNRATE) or plain words ("core inflation", "10 year treasury yield").

transform.description: level (default), change from the previous observation, pct_change (fraction), or yoy (fraction against the value a year earlier).

last.description: Only the most recent n observations.

tools.name: price_history
tools.description: Price bars (open, high, low, close, volume), daily to hourly, for US stocks and ETFs, stocks listed abroad (SAP.DE, 7203.T), currency pairs (EUR/USD), futures (crude oil, gold), indices and yields (S&P 500, VIX, 10 year yield) and crypto (bitcoin), by symbol or plain name. Stocks adjust for splits and dividends by default, with dividends, splits and the total return; returns: true adds daily returns. No key needed; uses the user's Alpaca or Tiingo key for US stocks when set.

symbol.description: A ticker (AAPL, BRK.B), a stock listed abroad with its market suffix (SAP.DE, 7203.T, SHEL.L, 0700.HK), a currency pair (EUR/USD), a future (CL=F, or "crude oil", "gold"), an index (^GSPC, or "S&P 500", "VIX", "10 year yield") or a crypto pair (BTC/USD, or "bitcoin").

start.description: First date; default one year ago.

returns.description: Also return simple returns from close to close (returns[i] is from dates[i] to dates[i+1]), ready for beta, correlation or Sharpe tools.

tools.name: fund_portfolio
tools.description: What a US mutual fund or ETF holds, from its own SEC Form N-PORT (VOO, IVV, QQQ, AGG, FXAIX): every position with value and weight, exposure by asset type, issuer, country and currency, a bond fund's coupon and maturity profile, its monthly returns, the money that came in and went out each month, and what changed since the previous quarter.

fund.description: A mutual fund or ETF ticker (VOO, IVV, QQQ, AGG, FXAIX, ARKK) or an SEC series id (S000004310).

period.description: Report date, the last day of a fiscal quarter's last month (2026-06-30); default the latest public one.

top.description: Most positions to list, by value; default 25.

compare.description: Also compare with the previous public report; default true.

tools.name: options_chain
tools.description: An option chain from Cboe's delayed data for a stock, ETF or index (AAPL, SPY, SPX, VIX): bids, asks, implied volatility, greeks, open interest and volume by strike for one expiration, every expiration with its open interest, put/call ratios, max pain and the move the at-the-money straddle prices in.

symbol.description: A stock or ETF (AAPL, SPY, QQQ) or an index (SPX, NDX, RUT, VIX, XSP).

expiration.description: An expiration date (2026-11-20), or "nearest" (default); the result lists every expiration.

window.description: Strikes within this fraction of the underlying price; default 0.1 (10 percent).

min_open_interest.description: Only contracts with at least this open interest; default 0.

tools.name: volatility_surface
tools.description: The implied volatility surface from Cboe's delayed option data: at-the-money IV by expiration (term structure), 25-delta put and call IV with the risk reversal and butterfly (skew), and IV at fixed moneyness from 80 to 120 percent of the price (smile).

symbol.description: A stock or ETF (AAPL, SPY) or an index (SPX, NDX, RUT, VIX).

expirations.description: How many expirations from the nearest; default 8.

tools.name: futures_curve
tools.description: A Cboe futures curve from its daily settlements: VIX futures by expiration with the VIX index, contango or backwardation and the front month's premium; also mini VIX, variance, bitcoin and iBoxx bond index futures.

product.description: A Cboe futures product: VIX (default), mini VIX, S&P 500 variance, bitcoin, or the iBoxx high yield, investment grade and emerging market bond index futures.

tools.name: segment_revenue
tools.description: Where a company's revenue comes from, read from the XBRL of its latest 10-K (or 10-Q): revenue and operating income by business segment, revenue by product or service and by region, for up to three years, with the company's own labels and each breakdown checked against total revenue.

form.description: Annual (10-K, default: fiscal years) or quarterly (10-Q: the quarter).

tools.name: index_constituents
tools.description: The members of a stock index (S&P 500, Nasdaq 100, Russell 2000, S&P 400, MSCI EAFE) with their weights, read from the N-PORT of an ETF that tracks it, with the report date, the number of members and how concentrated the top ten are.

index.description: An index by name ("S&P 500", "Nasdaq 100", "Russell 2000", "S&P 400", "MSCI EAFE"), or the ticker of an ETF that tracks the index you want (VOO, IWM).

limit.description: Most members to list, by weight; default 50.

tools.name: fomc
tools.description: The Federal Reserve's rate decisions from its own record: each FOMC meeting of a year (held and scheduled), the action, change and target range, the vote with dissenters and their reasons, links to statements and minutes, the latest statement, and the median projections (dot plot) for GDP, unemployment, inflation and the federal funds rate.

year.description: Meetings and decisions of this year; default this year.

tools.name: economic_calendar
tools.description: The US economic calendar from the agencies' own schedules: when BLS (jobs, CPI, PPI, JOLTS), BEA (GDP, personal income and PCE, trade), the Census Bureau (retail sales, housing starts, durable goods) and the Fed (FOMC decisions) release, with times in US Eastern and the market-moving releases flagged.

until.description: Last date; default 30 days after since.

key_only.description: Only the releases markets watch most (jobs, CPI, PPI, JOLTS, GDP, PCE, retail sales, housing starts, durable goods, trade, the employment cost index, FOMC decisions).

tools.name: executive_pay
tools.description: What a company's executives are paid against how it did, from the pay-versus-performance table in its proxy: the CEO's reported pay and the pay actually earned, the other executives' averages, shareholder return against peers, net income and the company's chosen measure, five years; or every company's CEO pay ranked, with mis-scaled filings held out.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name. Without it, every company that tagged a pay-versus-performance table for the year, ranked.

year.description: Across the market, the fiscal year (by calendar year); default last year.

rank_by.description: Across the market: the CEO's reported pay (default), pay actually paid, or total shareholder return.

limit.description: Across the market, most companies to list; default 25.

tools.name: short_interest
tools.description: Short interest in US stocks from FINRA, twice a month: shares short, the change, average daily volume and days to cover over several reports, and the share of shares outstanding from the company's latest SEC cover page; or, with no stock, the market ranked by days to cover, change or size.

symbol.description: A US stock ticker. Without it, the whole market at the latest settlement date, ranked.

periods.description: Settlement dates to show for a stock, newest last; default 6 (three months).

rank_by.description: Across the market: days to cover (default), the change since the last report, or shares short.

min_volume.description: Across the market, only stocks averaging at least this many shares a day; default 1,000,000, so thin stocks do not crowd the list.

limit.description: Across the market, most stocks to list; default 25.

tools.name: off_exchange_volume
tools.description: How much of a US stock trades away from the exchanges, from FINRA's OTC transparency data: weekly shares and trades in dark pools (ATSs) and with other off-exchange dealers, and the largest dark pools and dealers in the latest week.

weeks.description: Weeks to show, newest last; default 8. FINRA publishes Tier 1 stocks two weeks after the week, others four.

tools.name: fails_to_deliver
tools.description: Shares that failed to settle, from the SEC's fails-to-deliver data (NSCC): a stock's outstanding fail balance on each settlement date over the latest half-month files, with prices and dollar values, or the securities with the largest fails across the market.

symbol.description: A ticker. Without it, the securities with the largest fails by value in the latest file.

files.description: Half-month files to read, newest first; default 2 (about a month) for a ticker, 1 across the market.

limit.description: Across the market, most securities to list; default 25.

tools.name: futures_positioning
tools.description: Who holds what in a futures market, from the CFTC's weekly Commitments of Traders: long, short and net positions of producers, swap dealers, managed money and others (or dealers, asset managers and leveraged funds for financial futures), with weekly changes and where the speculators sit in their range, by market name (gold, crude oil, 10 year note, euro, bitcoin).

market.description: A futures market by name ("gold", "crude oil", "corn", "s&p 500", "10 year note", "euro", "bitcoin", "vix") or a CFTC contract market code (088691).

weeks.description: Weekly reports to return, newest last; default 52.

tools.name: private_offerings
tools.description: Private markets from Form D, filed when startups and funds sell securities without registering: amount offered and sold, number of investors, minimum investment, exemption (Rule 506(b) or 506(c)), industry, fund type and the people behind it, for one issuer or across the market (newest first, filtered by industry or amount sold).

company.description: An issuer by name or CIK (a startup, a fund). Without it, the latest Form D filings across the market.

industry.description: Across the market, keep issuers whose Form D industry group contains these words: "Pooled Investment Fund", "Biotechnology", "Other Technology", "Real Estate", "Banking".

min_sold.description: Across the market, keep offerings that have sold at least this many dollars.

since.description: Filed on or after this date; default seven days ago across the market, ten years for an issuer.

limit.description: Most offerings to list; default 20. Across the market at most 100 filings are read to find them.

tools.name: company_events
tools.description: Company news from the source: the events companies must report on Form 8-K (earnings, deals, executive changes, restatements, auditor changes, bankruptcies, cyber incidents, layoffs, delisting notices), for one company or, by event, across the whole market, each with the headline of the press release it attached and the opening of what the filing says.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name. Without it, filings across the whole market (then event is required).

event.description: Which events: an item number (2.02) or a name: earnings, material_agreement, acquisition_or_sale_completed, executive_change, restatement, auditor_change, bankruptcy, cybersecurity_incident, restructuring, impairment, delisting_notice, new_debt, shareholder_vote, regulation_fd, other_event. Default: all, for a company.

since.description: Filed on or after this date; default 180 days ago for a company, 30 days across the market.

until.description: Filed on or before this date; default today.

excerpts.description: Read each filing for the opening of what it says and its press release's headline; default true (up to three requests per filing).

tools.name: latest_filings
tools.description: What has just been filed with the SEC, across every company: EDGAR's latest-filings feed, newest first by acceptance time, filtered by form (8-K, 10-K, 4, SC 13D, S-1...), 8-K event (earnings, executive change, restatement, bankruptcy), words in the filer's name and time. For watching what comes in today and over the last few business days; list_filings and company_events reach further back.

forms.description: Form types, e.g. ["8-K"], ["10-K", "10-Q"], ["4"], ["SC 13D"], ["S-1"]; each also matches its amendments (8-K/A). Default: every form.

event.description: 8-K filings with this item only: an item number (2.02) or a name (earnings, executive_change, restatement, bankruptcy, cybersecurity_incident...).

company.description: Words that must all appear in the filer's name, e.g. "bancorp" or "apple".

since.description: Accepted at or after this time (a date means its start, US Eastern). Default: everything the feed holds.

tools.name: filing_diff
tools.description: What changed in a company's 10-K (or 10-Q) against the one before, section by section (risk factors by default, MD&A, business, legal proceedings): new and dropped paragraphs, the sentences changed in the rest, and the words whose use rose or fell most.

section.description: The item to compare: "risk factors" (default), "md&a", "business", "legal proceedings", "market risk", "1A"...

form.description: Default 10-K: the latest annual report against the one before.

accession.description: The newer filing; default the latest.

against.description: The older filing; default the one filed before the newer.

threshold.description: Word-pair overlap at which two paragraphs are the same paragraph. Default 0.5.

max_items.description: Most new, dropped and changed paragraphs listed each. Default 8; raise it to read more.

tools.name: news
tools.description: News about a company or a topic from the world's press (the GDELT Project's open index, no key): articles newest first with outlet and country, and the daily average tone of the coverage.

query.description: Words or a "quoted phrase" to find, e.g. "\"rate cut\" Fed". With company, they narrow its news.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name: its news, searched by the company's name.

start.description: Instead of days: the first day (GDELT's search covers about the last three months).

end.description: With start: the last day (default start).

language.description: Source language, e.g. english (default) or any; others by name (german, japanese...).

tone.description: Add the daily average tone of the coverage (one more request, about five seconds). Default true.

tools.name: explain_move
tools.description: Why a stock moved on a day, in one call: its return against the market and how rare it was for this stock (a market model fitted on the year before, with a z-score), the company's SEC filings around the day (8-K items named), and the press's headlines from those days.

date.description: The trading day of the move (YYYY-MM-DD).

benchmark.description: The market to compare with; default SPY.

window_days.description: Calendar days either side of the date for filings and news; default 2.

news.description: Add the press's headlines (GDELT, about five seconds). Default true.

tools.name: portfolio_xray
tools.description: A portfolio seen through its funds: each ETF or mutual fund opened into the positions of its latest SEC N-PORT and added to the stocks held directly, giving the real exposure to each company, the overlap between funds and the effective number of positions.

symbol.description: A stock (AAPL) or a fund or ETF (VOO, QQQ, AGG, FXAIX).

weight.description: Its weight or its value: weights are rescaled to sum to 1.

top.description: Most look-through positions to list; default 25.

tools.name: comps
tools.description: A comparable-companies table: the company beside its NYSE- and Nasdaq-listed peers in the same SEC industry code, the nearest in revenue, on revenue, growth, margins, ROE, R&D intensity and FCF margin (or measures you pick), with the peers' median and the company's rank on each.

metrics.description: Measures to compare; default revenue, growth, margins, ROE, R&D intensity and FCF margin.

peers.description: Peers to show, nearest in revenue; default 8.

period.description: FY2025: each company's fiscal year that best overlaps calendar 2025 (the default is the last complete year).

fiscal_year_end.description: Instead of period: each company's fiscal year ending in this window (slower: more data to read).

tools.name: debt_profile
tools.description: A company's debt from its annual reports' XBRL: total and net debt, the maturity ladder from the debt note (next 12 months to after five years), lease payments, interest expense, the implied interest rate, interest coverage and debt to EBITDA, with five years of debt and cash.

years.description: Annual history of total debt and cash to show; default 5.

tools.name: ownership_breadth
tools.description: How many institutions hold a stock, quarter by quarter: 13F filers whose holdings tables list its CUSIP (EDGAR full-text search), with the change and a sample of holders. A fall in breadth predicted lower returns (Chen, Hong and Stein 2002).

cusip.description: Or the share class's 9-character CUSIP (037833100 for Apple).

quarters.description: Quarters of 13F filings to count, newest first; default 6.

holders.description: Filers to list from the latest quarter; default 20.

tools.name: forensic_scores
tools.description: Three accounting screens in one call from the company's own annual XBRL for its last two years: Beneish's M-score (earnings manipulation), Piotroski's F-score (financial strength) and Altman's Z-score (distress), every input with its tag.

tools.name: funding_rates
tools.description: Crypto perpetual funding on OKX's USDT perpetuals, no key: each coin's latest eight-hour rate, the window's mean and its annualized carry (short the perpetual against long spot), the last week's, and the share of positive periods.

coins.description: Coin symbols, e.g. ["BTC", "ETH", "SOL"]; default BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE.

days.description: Window, in days back from now; default 30.

series.description: Also return each coin's funding by period; default false.

tools.name: large_holders
tools.description: Who owns more than 5 percent of a company, from Schedules 13D and 13G: each holder's latest stake (shares, percent of class, voting power), whether it is passive (13G) or may seek to influence control (13D, with its stated purpose); or, with no company, the newest 13D stakes across the whole market.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name. Without it, the latest filings across the whole market (new activist stakes by default).

schedule.description: 13D (may seek to influence control; states its purpose), 13G (passive) or both. Default: both for a company, 13D across the market.

since.description: Filed on or after this date; default three years ago for a company, seven days ago across the market.

tools.name: earnings_calendar
tools.description: Earnings dates from the companies' own 8-Ks (Item 2.02, results of operations). For a company: its recent results releases with the quarter each covered and whether it came before the open or after the close (EDGAR's acceptance time), and the next release estimated from the same quarter a year earlier, with a window. Across the market: who is due to report in a window, from when they reported in the same weeks last year, marked once they have. Estimates, not announcements.

company.description: Ticker, CIK or name: its results releases and the next one estimated. Leave out for the market.

quarters.description: Past releases to list for a company; default 8.

since.description: Across the market: first day of the window; default today.

until.description: Across the market: last day; default 14 days after since, at most 31.

limit.description: Across the market: most companies to list (the largest first); default 100.

tools.name: investment_advisers
tools.description: Investment advisers from the SEC's Form ADV database (IAPD) by name or CRD: matching firms with SEC file numbers, status, whether they report disclosure events, offices and branch counts, then the best match in full: registration and since when, other names and relying advisers, its latest ADV date, and links to its Form ADV and brochures.

query.description: A firm's name ("Bridgewater Associates", "Renaissance Technologies") or its CRD number (105129).

limit.description: Most matching firms to list for a name; default 10.

tools.name: world_economy
tools.description: Any country's or region's economy from the World Bank's World Development Indicators (200+ countries, the euro area, the world, income groups): GDP and growth, inflation, unemployment, government debt and deficits, the current account, trade, reserves, interest rates, population and more, by plain words or indicator code, as a year-by-country table with each country's latest value.

indicator.description: Plain words ("gdp growth", "inflation", "government debt", "current account", "unemployment") or a World Bank indicator code (NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG).

countries.description: Countries or regions: names ("Germany", "euro area", "world") or ISO codes (US, DEU).

start.description: First year; default ten years before end.

end.description: Last year; default this year (the latest year is often not yet published).

tools.name: economic_outlook
tools.description: The OECD's projections for the next two years from its Economic Outlook, for 50+ economies, the euro area, the OECD and the world: GDP growth, inflation (harmonised for the euro area), core inflation, unemployment, budget balance, government debt, current account and short- and long-term interest rates, beside its estimates for the two years before.

countries.description: Countries or groups: names ("Germany", "euro area", "world", "OECD") or ISO codes (US, JPN).

measures.description: What to project: "gdp growth", "inflation", "core inflation", "unemployment", "budget balance", "government debt", "current account", "short term interest rate", "long term interest rate". Default: GDP growth, inflation, unemployment.

tools.name: treasury_auctions
tools.description: US Treasury auction results, or the auctions announced next, from the Treasury itself: bills, notes, bonds, TIPS and FRNs by term ("10-year", "13-week bill"), with the rate each cleared at, coupon, bid-to-cover, size and the shares taken by indirect bidders (foreign and other), direct bidders and primary dealers, plus averages to compare the latest auction with recent ones.

security.description: Which securities: "10-year", "2-year note", "30-year bond", "13-week bill", "5-year TIPS", "2-year FRN", or a kind ("bills", "notes", "bonds", "tips"). Default: all.

upcoming.description: Announced auctions not yet held, soonest first, instead of results.

since.description: Results from this auction date; default 180 days ago.

until.description: Results up to this auction date; default today.

tools.name: federal_debt
tools.description: The US federal debt each business day from the Treasury's Debt to the Penny (total, held by the public, intragovernmental) over any window since 1993, its change over the window, and the average interest rate the Treasury pays on each type of security.

start.description: First date; default one year ago.

frequency.description: daily, or monthly (the last reported day of each month); default daily up to two years, monthly beyond.

instructions: Market data and research from the public sources themselves. Before answering with a company's reported figures, check them with verify_claims: each comes back confirmed, contradicted (with the filed figure and what the wrong one matches) or not reported. Across the market: screen_companies ranks every US-listed company on fundamentals, company_report gives one company's financials, segment_revenue its revenue by segment, product and region, valuation, risk, insiders and filings in one call, event_study measures price reactions to earnings or insider trades, mentions_trend counts a phrase in filings over time. Analyst work: financial_statements gives the income statement, balance sheet and cash flows exactly as filed (several years joined, restatements and splits shown, never mixed); filing_tables finds the table that holds a figure in a filing, or follows it through several years of filings (members, stores, ARPU, guidance tables); earnings_release reads a results press release: results, guidance as ranges, and last quarter's guidance against this quarter's results. Companies: company_profile, list_filings, then read_filing (section "risk factors", "md&a" and so on for a 10-K or 10-Q; document "EX-99.1" for an 8-K press release); search_filings finds words across all filings; executive_pay reads a proxy's pay-versus-performance table; company_events gives a company's 8-K news (or, by event, the whole market's: restatements, bankruptcies, cyber incidents); latest_filings is what has just been filed, across every company, by form and event; filing_diff shows what changed in a 10-K's risk factors (or any item) since the last one; news gives the world's press coverage of a company or topic, with its tone; explain_move puts a day's move beside the filings and headlines around it; portfolio_xray opens a portfolio's funds into the companies they hold; comps sets a company beside its industry peers; debt_profile gives its debt, when it falls due and what it costs; ownership_breadth counts the institutions holding it, quarter by quarter; forensic_scores runs the Beneish, Piotroski and Altman screens on its filings. earnings_calendar gives a company's results dates and the next one estimated, or who reports in a window. Ownership: insider_trades (Form 4) and fund_holdings (a manager's 13F); large_holders (13D/13G: 5 percent holders and activists), investment_advisers (Form ADV); funds: fund_portfolio (what a mutual fund or ETF holds, its flows and returns, from N-PORT); private markets: private_offerings (Form D raises by startups and funds); positioning: short_interest, off_exchange_volume (FINRA dark pools), fails_to_deliver (SEC) and futures_positioning (CFTC Commitments of Traders). Rates and the economy: economic_calendar (when the data comes out), fomc (the Fed's decisions, votes and projections), treasury_yields, treasury_auctions, federal_debt, economic_series (FRED), world_economy (World Bank, every country) and economic_outlook (OECD projections). Beyond the US: european_filings (a company's ESEF annual report, the figures it tagged), reference_rates (SOFR, EFFR, €STR, ECB and Bank of England rates from the central banks, and about forty central banks' policy rates), prediction_markets (Polymarket and Kalshi prices for an outcome) and crypto_fundamentals (DefiLlama: a protocol's value locked, fees and revenue, a chain's value locked, a stablecoin's supply) and funding_rates (perpetual funding and its annualized carry, OKX). Options: options_chain, volatility_surface and futures_curve (Cboe delayed data). Prices: price_history for stocks in the US and abroad, currencies, futures, indices and crypto (no key needed; the user's Alpaca or Tiingo key is used for US stocks when set). Every result has its source URL; cite it.
